news.headline: Scientists Find the First Green Star!
news.body: Astronomers at the University of Warwick in England studied white dwarfs, the tiny, super-dense cores left over when stars like our Sun run out of fuel. They found that some would look pink, purple, yellow or pale blue up close, depending on what is in their air. One star, called WD J1330+6435, would glow a lime green. It is the first green star anyone has ever found! The scientists think about 1 in 30 white dwarfs shine an unusual color.

news.headline: Six Rare Piglets Make Zoo History
news.body: The North Carolina Zoo welcomed six Visayan warty piglets, a very rare kind of pig. Fewer than 200 are thought to live in the wild, only on two small islands in the Philippines. One mom, Buddy, had four piglets at once, the biggest litter on record for her kind in zoos. They are the first of these piglets born in the United States since 2022. Visitors can meet them when the zoo's new Asia area opens next March.

news.headline: A 12-Year-Old Becomes a Go-Kart World Champion
news.body: Jack Miller, a 12-year-old from Northern Ireland, won a world championship for small go-karts in Spain. He worked his way to the front, stayed calm, and crossed the finish line first. Karting is where many famous race car drivers got their start. Jack dreams of racing sports cars one day. Getting his giant trophy home was tricky, too: it had to be wrapped in clothes and squeezed into the biggest suitcase!

fun_fact: The Sun is actually white! It looks yellow from the ground because Earth's air scatters some of its blue light across the sky. ☀️

word_of_the_day.meaning: packed tightly, with a lot of stuff squeezed into a small space
word_of_the_day.sentence: A white dwarf star is so dense that it can hold about as much stuff as our Sun in a ball the size of Earth.

this_day_in_history: On October 19, 2017, a telescope in Hawaii spotted 'Oumuamua, the first object ever seen visiting our solar system from beyond it.
did_you_know: Pigs can hardly sweat at all, so they roll around in mud to stay cool. The mud also works like sunscreen for their skin! 🐖
